title: Thin plate strip thickness and Poisson sensitivity
source: Kirchhoff thin-plate bending theory, D=E t^3/[12(1-nu^2)], with the discrete shell strip used as the numerical realization. The reference ratios are the closed-form bending ratios; the stated bands cover shear deformation and the four-by-one mesh.

quantities.quantity: t times tip deflection derivative divided by deflection
quantities.reason: Kirchhoff bending gives w proportional to t^-3; the 50% band covers transverse shear and coarse mesh effects.

quantities.quantity: t times first frequency derivative divided by frequency
quantities.reason: With shell mass proportional to t and bending stiffness proportional to t^3, thin-plate theory gives f proportional to t; the band covers shear and mesh effects.

quantities.quantity: nu times tip deflection derivative divided by deflection
quantities.reason: Kirchhoff plate theory gives -2 nu^2/(1-nu^2); the 80% band explicitly covers the dominant shear and coarse-mesh departure in this four-by-one strip.

quantities.quantity: nu times first frequency derivative divided by frequency
quantities.reason: The thin-plate frequency ratio is nu^2/(1-nu^2); the wide band covers the coarse strip and shear terms.
